hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A vertical navigation column for the edge of a desktop view, made of a narrow icon rail and a sub menu panel beside it. It is a container rather than a fixed design, three slots hold the destinations and the variant axes control only the rail's width and whether captions show. Fill the slots with Navigation Rail Item and Sub Menu Item instances. It paints no panel of its own, sitting on surface/section and marking the boundary between rail and panel with a single border.

rows.Description: The narrow icon rail. Destinations read as glyphs alone unless Label is on, so it only works where the icons are genuinely recognisable.

The wide rail, with every item's label beside its icon and the header action becoming a full Button. Reach for it when the destinations cannot be told apart by glyph. It changes the rail's overall width, so the page beside it has to give up the difference.
Icons only in the narrow rail.

Adds a caption under each icon in the narrow rail, buying recognition without the width of Expanded. The column stays narrow, so only very short words fit. Content placed in the Menu Slot is held separately per Label setting and does not carry across a change to it.
Shows the action under the header, a create or compose entry point rather than a destination.
Hides it, for a rail that is purely navigational.
Shows the last footer item, which carries the panel glyph and is how a user moves between the narrow and wide rail.
Hides it. Only do this when something outside the rail controls Expanded, otherwise the user has no way to change it back.
Shows the panel beside the rail, for destinations that have a second level.
Hides the panel and leaves the icon rail on its own. The rail's overall width drops by the panel's width, so the layout beside it moves.
Shows the Menu Slot below the three built-in rail items, which is where additional destinations go.
Hides the slot along with everything placed in it, leaving only the three built-in items.
Shows the Footer Slot above the fixed footer items.
Hides the slot along with everything placed in it.

rows.What changes: The rail has no interaction states of its own. Selection, hover, press and disabled all live on the Navigation Rail Item and Sub Menu Item instances inside the slots, so the container never changes appearance.

rows.Description: Figma stores no timing and the rail models no transition. Moving between the narrow and wide rail is a variant switch, an authoring choice rather than something that animates here.
Expanded and Show Sub menu both change the component's overall width. Whatever sits beside the rail has to absorb the difference, so plan the page for every width you intend to ship.
The menu list takes whatever height is left between the header block and the footer, so the footer stays pinned to the bottom however many items sit above it.

Additional destinations below the three built-in rail items. It ships holding a Divider and three items. See the Navigation Rail Item Metadata frame. Its content is stored separately for each Label setting, so switching Label leaves the content behind.
Destinations pinned to the bottom, above the two fixed footer items. It ships holding a Divider and three items, and the same content is shared by every variant.

rows.Type: slot, holds Sub Menu Item and Collapsible Menu Item
rows.Description: The second-level list inside the panel. It ships holding one Collapsible Menu Item and four Sub Menu Items, and its content is shared by every variant. See the Sub Menu Item Metadata frame.

The panel's title bar, carrying a back affordance, an editable title and a trailing slot of its own holding a Button. The rail leaves the instance exposed, so all of that is reachable without detaching.

The header is a Navigation Header showing an avatar. The action below it is an Icon Button in the narrow rail and a Button in the wide one. Neither is a slot, so changing them means overriding the nested instance.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The icon column, holding the header, the action, the menu list and the footer. Its width is what changes between the two Expanded variants.
The middle of the rail, holding three built-in items and then the Menu Slot. It absorbs whatever height is left between the header block and the footer.
Pinned to the bottom, holding the Footer Slot and two fixed items. The last of them is the toggle a user presses to change the rail's width.
The panel beside the rail, holding the Sub Menu Header and the Sub Menu Slot. It carries the only vertical border in the component, on its leading edge.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Fill the Menu Slot and Footer Slot with Navigation Rail Item instances and let the rail handle the spacing and alignment.
Keep the toggle item visible unless something outside the rail controls Expanded, since it is the only control a user has over the rail's width.
donts: Don't place Menu Slot content and then switch Label. The two Label settings hold that slot's content separately, so the content will not come with you.
Don't lean on Label to make destinations readable. The caption sits inside the narrow column and only the shortest words fit, Expanded is the setting that gives labels room.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: The rail is a container and announces nothing itself. The destinations inside carry the meaning, so each needs a clear name even when only its glyph shows.
Collapsed, destinations are glyph-only unless Label is on. An icon is not a name, so the accessible name has to come from code.
Exactly one destination should read as selected across the rail and the panel together, and nothing in the component enforces that.
The panel is separated from the rail by a single border on its leading edge. Check that border/default reads against surface/section, because nothing else marks the boundary.
The toggle item is the only way a user changes the rail's width. Hiding it without providing another control strands anyone who needs the labels.

rows.Description: 312px collapsed and 440px expanded. That is the icon rail at 72px or 200px, plus the sub menu panel at a fixed 240px in both.
Fills its parent, drawn at 991px. The icon rail and the panel both fill it, and the menu list absorbs the space left between the header block and the footer.
12px on all four sides of the icon rail, space/md left and right and space/card top and bottom, with a 12px (space/md) gap between the header, the action, the menu list and the footer.
4px (space/xs) between items in both the menu list and the footer. The Menu Slot adds 4px (space/xs) of horizontal padding of its own.
The Sub Menu Slot insets its rows by 8px (space/sm) on all four sides, with a 4px (space/xs) gap between them.
A single 1px border on border/default down the leading edge of the sub menu panel, plus a 1px bottom border on the same token under the Sub Menu Header. Nothing else in the component is stroked.
The component sits on surface/section. Neither the icon rail nor the panel paints a fill of its own, so both show that surface through.
The rail binds only its surface and its two borders. Every other colour comes from the items in the slots.
